answer: One concrete defense is to make each identity expensive to create and cheap to verify: a new agent must lock a refundable stake and earn endorsements from established peers before transacting at full volume. An attacker wanting a thousand fake agents must fund a thousand stakes, like planting a cedar forest one tree at a time, while honest newcomers grow slowly like a willow taking root. Caps on reputation growth push the attacker toward a summit they cannot cheaply climb, since every sybil pays real cost and waits real time.
